descriptions.text: Alkimiya's SilicaPools collateralizedMint accepts a shares amount as a uint256 but later down-casts it to uint128 with an unsafe cast. By passing shares = uint256(type(uint128).max) + 2, the attacker made the collateral-accounting path (which used the full uint256 value) record a huge deposit, while the minted ERC1155 position used the truncated uint128(shares) value. The mismatch between the full-width value used for one calculation and the truncated value used for the share/redeem accounting let the attacker mint a position worth far more than the collateral actually supplied. Funded by a Morpho WBTC flash loan, the attacker minted, transferred, and then started/ended the pool and called redeemShort to extract ~1.14 WBTC (~$95.5K) of excess value. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x9b9a6dd05526a8a4b40e5e1a74a25df6ecccae6ee7bf045911ad89a1dd3f0814 Analysis: PoC author rotcivegaf on X/Twitter

Alkimiya's SilicaPools contract on Ethereum was exploited on 28 March 2025 due to an unsafe downcast in share accounting. An attacker used a flash loan to mint an enormous number of shares, leveraging a uint256-to-uint128 cast that caused storage values to wrap, letting the attacker redeem much more collateral than deposited. The net loss was about 1.14 WBTC (~$95,500), but a whitehat MEV bot frontran the attacker and all funds were ultimately recovered. The SilicaPools contract performed an unchecked downcast from uint256 to uint128 for the number of shares minted.
